A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GRALE and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably across the revised layout and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, ablation, downstream prediction, graph-matching, and representation-analysis results in Sections 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds GraphMAE comparisons, matcher fine-tuning results, Bayesian-network regression, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The core architecture and reconstruction loss remain unchanged. v2 adds matcher fine-tuning on random training-graph pairs and a BN adaptation combining the lightweight GIN encoder and Transformer decoder previously described as ablation alternatives.

E1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds unsupervised training and BIC-score regression on 200,000 eight-node Bayesian networks, extending coverage to a distinct domain beyond molecules and COLORING. Existing benchmark coverage remains. Larger-graph resource profiling does not establish additional predictive-task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds GraphMAE to the existing molecular comparisons. New Table 11 compares GRALE with GraphRNN, GCN, DeepGMG, S-VAE, and D-VAE on BN, substantially expanding the comparator suite. Those BN baseline scores are explicitly taken from cited work, rather than reported as reruns.

E3.justification: Added evaluations introduce BN pretraining followed by MLP regression using RMSE and Pearson's r, random-pair matcher fine-tuning, and single-gradient-step profiling with batch size 1 across N=8–256. The established benchmark splits and Table 9 training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the PCA/t-SNE embedding-structure analysis from v1 Section 5.2 and Figure 4. It adds training-cost comparisons, graph-size sensitivity of time and memory, and a comparison with matcher fine-tuning. Existing component ablations, denoising, data/latent-size analyses, and reconstruction failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Five-run ablations, five downstream train/test splits, and mean/standard-deviation reporting over 1,000 graph pairs remain unchanged. Added rows reuse existing reporting practices; the new BN and resource tables introduce no additional repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds GraphMAE results, including BBBP ROC-AUC 0.773 versus GRALE's unchanged 0.731. Table 5 adds fine-tuned matching distances 7.64/19.33 alongside unchanged untuned values 8.92/32.77. Table 4 swaps QM9 edit distances: Any2Graph changes 2.13 to 2.61 and fine-tuned GRALE 2.61 to 2.13, reversing their reported ranking. Tables 10–12 add training costs, BN results (RMSE 0.18, r=0.98), and resource measurements. The embedding-projection findings are removed.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–4 and their proofs remain unchanged. Section 2.1 removes the explicit zero-loss-if-and-only-if-equality qualification from its complexity statement. New Appendix C asserts cubic memory as well as time complexity, and Table 10 adds comparative theoretical complexity bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about variable-size graph autoencoding, learned matching with an optimal-transport-inspired loss, Evoformer-based encoding/decoding, and broad downstream applicability.

C2.justification: v2 develops the earlier suggestion of adapting GRALE to smaller datasets into a demonstrated lightweight BN application. Appendix C clarifies that N=32 is not a strict limit and estimates resources for N=128. Section 5.3 introduces fine-tuning as a remedy for the matcher's training/test distribution mismatch.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, GRALE/Sinkhorn pseudocode, BN architecture and hyperparameter cross-references, and hardware/configuration details for resource profiling. The main training settings and the 100-step log-domain Sinkhorn implementation were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for GraphMAE, D-VAE, and neural set divergence, replaces the graph-complexity reference, and explicitly connects the matcher to linear assignment of learned node embeddings. The central positioning relative to PIGVAE and Any2Graph remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short architecture overview, Appendix B.4, and a complexity appendix, shifting the former Appendices C–F to D–G. Local prose, headings, affiliations, and conference information change, while the projection-analysis passage is removed. Most language and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Figures 1–2 are redesigned or relabeled, Figure 3's color scale changes, and v1 Figure 4 is removed. v2 adds two algorithm panels and Tables 10–12, expands Tables 3 and 5, and relocates several existing displays.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evidence on domain transfer and computational requirements, broadens baseline comparisons, and improves implementation/access documentation. These gains are limited by removal of the embedding visualization and insufficient BN split and matcher fine-tuning details. The retained autoencoder-superiority statement also needs qualification: newly added GraphMAE exceeds GRALE on both classification tasks in Table 3.
